title: Tobacco rose the most since 2000
body: Prices for tobacco are up 837% since 2000 — the steepest climb of any item in the basket. Over the same period the overall CPI rose 97%.

title: 14 things are actually cheaper than in 2000
body: Not everything gets dearer. 14 items cost less than they did in 2000 — led by audio, visual and computing equipment (-90%). Falling technology and clothing prices quietly offset the rises.

title: Rising fastest right now: Electricity
body: In the year to September 2025, electricity rose 23.6% — the fastest annual increase in the basket, against overall inflation of 3.2%.

title: Falling fastest right now: Small electric household appliances
body: Small electric household appliances fell 4.5% over the year to September 2025 — the biggest annual price drop in the basket.

title: The wildest ride: Child care
body: Child care has the most volatile price of any item — its annual inflation has swung between -95% and +2009%. Weather, fuel and global supply make it lurch.

title: Inflation isn't the same in every city
body: Over the year to September 2025, prices rose fastest in Brisbane (4.7%) and slowest in Adelaide (2.4%) — a 2.3 point gap between capitals.

title: Wages have not kept up with prices
body: Since 2020, wages rose 20.2% while prices rose 23.6% — a real change in buying power of -2.7%. A pay rise that trails inflation is a pay cut in real terms.

title: The shrinking dollar
body: A dollar in 2000 buys about 51c worth of goods today — you now need $1.97 to buy what $1 bought in 2000. Since 1948, prices are up more than 38-fold.
